dedupe_keys.name: delaware fire station accessibility under probabilistic flood road failures and sea level rise

description: This case study measures how road flooding cuts access from neighbourhoods to fire stations in the US state of Delaware, and how that burden falls on socially vulnerable communities. Jiaji Ma, Utkarsh Gangwal and Shangjia Dong of the University of Delaware and the University of Virginia presented it in an ASCE conference paper published in November 2023. The framework combines physical and social vulnerability: neighbourhoods are nodes in the road network, probabilistic flood scenarios are generated from FEMA flood risk maps, and a Monte Carlo simulation measures reachability and travel time to the closest fire station and to the station assigned by coverage area. The conference paper is available online from ASCE by purchase; its abstract is free in OpenAlex. Coverage is the state of Delaware. Caveats: flood scenarios come from FEMA maps, not hydrodynamic modelling, and the network data and results are not published separately. The authors propose an accessibility metric to guide fire station siting and service boundaries for more equitable flood risk management as sea levels rise. Simulation uses: a method and state-wide setting for flood-induced loss of emergency service access, for network accessibility and equity models. Related records: the fire station service areas data (data-fire-station-service-areas-p02647) and the Jakarta fire service isochrone gaps (data-jakarta-fire-service-isochrone-gaps) describe fire station coverage elsewhere.
